# Search Console API

*Tool*

The programming interface for reading Search Console data, such as performance and URL inspection, outside the web interface.

Narrative: the topic [Working with Search Console data](../topics/search-console-data.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

8 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 5 shown or said at the event (2 consistent with Google docs, 3 nothing to verify), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [API Reference](https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/api_reference_index), [Prerequisites](https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/prereqs).

- [`D1-C266`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Docs: To use the Search Console API you need a Google Account with Search Console permission on the property, a project in the Google API Console and OAuth2 credentials (all Search Console APIs except the Testing Tools API need OAuth2). `[D1-C266, docs, Google Search Console API documentation, https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/prereqs]`
- [`D1-C267`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Docs: Google states that all use of the Search Console API is free of charge but subject to usage limits. `[D1-C267, docs, Google Search Console API documentation, https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/pricing]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C462`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google said it knew of no plans to add crawl stats to the Search Console API, because that would be a completely new part of the API. `[D1-C462, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C463`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: A Google panelist said adding a report that is a variation of the Performance report to the Search Console API would be easier than adding crawl stats, because the Performance report is already in the API. `[D1-C463, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C255`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A community speaker who is not a developer automated monthly SEO reports with Python in Visual Studio Code, using Claude and ChatGPT as coding partners and Google Cloud for access to the Search Console API. `[D1-C255, stage, Kira Breuer, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C461`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: An audience member asked whether and when crawl stats will be added to the Search Console API. `[D1-C461, stage, an audience member, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C464`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: Google's Search Relations team talks with the Search Console team about the API more than before, partly because with so many vibe-coded systems around it is very easy to just say 'use the Search Console API to do something', and it is annoying when Search Console has no API for that. `[D1-C464, stage, Google, Day 1]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C268`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Analysis: Author's view: the Search Console API itself costs nothing, so the cost check advised on stage before automating reports is about the API's usage limits and the paid parts of the pipeline, such as storage and AI model calls. `[D1-C268, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
